title: SommBench: Assessing Sommelier Expertise of Language Models

model.params_source: paper Sec. 4 (zero-shot, temperature 0, single run); max_tokens assumed

items.columns_verified: question, a, b, c, d, level, true_label (lowercase a-d), language (codes en, sk, sv, fi, de, da, it, es; 128 rows each = 1,024)

prompt.verbatim: full (line-break hyphenations in the two-column extraction rejoined; typographic apostrophes normalised); machine form: user_template holds the English block, the other seven language blocks (unchanged) are in user_template_by_language keyed by the dataset's language code

output.postprocess: strip, uppercase; compare with true_label; unparsable counts as incorrect
output.parse_prose: letter (A-D): first standalone letter A-D in the reply

metric.name: accuracy
metric.definition: overall WTQA accuracy = mean of the eight per-language accuracies (equal-sized sets, so equal to the accuracy over all 1,024 items)
metric.alternative_cell: Table 2 (per-language WTQA accuracy), row gpt-4.1-nano, column EN = 0.80 (n = 128); SK 0.69, SV 0.74, FI 0.73, DE 0.72, DA 0.72, IT 0.74, ES 0.73

cost.prepare_note: runner --prepare 2026-09-07: est_usd_prepare counts <=400 output tokens per free-text call (runner out_guess); est_usd_dryrun_max_tokens counts the full max_tokens

notes: Very cheap (~$0.0005 per call). Reasoning traces are ignored for reasoning models (not relevant here). The released sommbench package implements the same prompts. || [hook 2026-09-07] render() selects prompt.user_template_by_language by the item's language code (Figures 4-11) and fills {question},{a},{b},{c},{d}; all 1,024 items (128 x 8 languages) run against Table 1 (0.73 = mean of the eight per-language accuracies; Table 2 gives the per-language cells, EN 0.80). Parse 'letter', label_map a-d -> A-D and accuracy stay with the runner.
